# UX & Accessibility Requirements Checklist: Application shell and cross-cutting UX

**Purpose**: Validate that the frame's visual, structural and accessibility requirements are complete, unambiguous and objectively verifiable before `/speckit-tasks`
**Created**: 2026-08-30
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope**: The frame as this feature renders it — sidebar, header, banner slot, content region, and the keyboard and assistive-technology surface of all four. Refusal semantics are in [authorization.md](authorization.md); rules inherited by later entries are in [conventions.md](conventions.md).

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the sidebar's height and its overflow behaviour specified, given that the project-list region grows unbounded once entry R5 fills it? [Gap, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK002 Is the user chip's position "at the foot" defined as pinned to the sidebar's bottom edge or as last in normal flow? The two differ once the entries above it overflow. [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK003 Are the header's own dimensions specified with the precision the sidebar's 262px receives, or is the asymmetry deliberate and recorded? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, §FR-001]
- [x] CHK004 Is the vertical origin of the content region specified for `/home`, the one authenticated screen that renders no header? [Gap, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK005 Is the banner slot's position stated as a requirement, or only under *Assumptions*, where an implementer is free to reinterpret it? [Traceability, Spec §FR-025, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK006 Are landmark and region semantics specified for the three shell areas, so that the frame is navigable by assistive technology and not only by keyboard? [Gap, Spec §FR-030, §FR-031]
- [x] CHK007 Is a bypass mechanism required for the sidebar, which repeats on every authenticated screen ahead of that screen's content? [Gap, Spec §FR-031, §SC-012]
- [x] CHK008 Is an accessible name required for the sidebar's navigation region so it is distinguishable from any other navigation a later entry adds? [Gap, Spec §FR-031]
- [x] CHK009 Is a target accessibility conformance level stated for this feature, or is SC-012's keyboard criterion the whole of the accessibility requirement? [Gap, Spec §SC-012, §FR-030]
- [x] CHK010 Is indication of the current screen within the sidebar specified as required, or as deliberately absent? The spec is silent while the plan records a decision. [Gap, Spec §FR-005, §FR-002]
- [x] CHK011 Are requirements defined for the shell's own first-paint or pending state, distinct from the per-screen skeletons FR-032 defers? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-032]

## Requirement Clarity & Measurability

- [x] CHK012 Is "chrome" defined precisely enough that a reviewer can judge whether an addition violates the rule? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK013 Can "one quiet line" be objectively verified — is the empty project-list wording fixed the way FR-022's wording is? [Measurability, Spec §FR-024]
- [x] CHK014 Is "visible focus indicator" given criteria that do not rest on colour alone? [Clarity, Spec §FR-031]
- [x] CHK015 Is "focus travels in visual order" defined relative to the document direction resolved for the request, given that FR-001 flips the sidebar's edge? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-031, §FR-001]
- [x] CHK016 Is "a suitable React Aria component" given a test an implementer and a reviewer would apply the same way? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-030]
- [x] CHK017 Is "the styling layer supplying appearance only" measurable — what counts as behaviour leaking into the styling layer? [Measurability, Spec §FR-030]
- [x] CHK018 Is the truncation point for a long display name specified, or only that truncation occurs? [Measurability, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-017]
- [x] CHK019 Is "the content region fills the remainder of the viewport" stated precisely enough to be checked at a given width? [Measurability, Spec §FR-009, §SC-001]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK020 Do FR-002's "entries unchanged from one screen to the next" and FR-016's role-driven change to those same entries reconcile explicitly, or must a reader infer the scope of each? [Conflict, Spec §FR-002, §FR-016]
- [x] CHK021 Is the precision of user-visible strings consistent — FR-022 and FR-035 quote their text verbatim while FR-019 and FR-024 describe theirs? [Consistency, Spec §FR-019, §FR-022, §FR-024, §FR-035]
- [x] CHK022 Are FR-008's project-scoped visibility rule and FR-013's disabled-with-reason rule consistent for a non-member on a project-scoped screen — does New issue render disabled, or not render? [Conflict, Spec §FR-008, §FR-013]
- [x] CHK023 Does the right-to-left requirement state what remains unchanged beyond the sidebar's edge, so "with nothing else about the frame changed" is checkable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, US1 s10]
- [x] CHK024 Do FR-003 (no header on Home) and FR-025 (banner on every screen, Home included) together fix a single unambiguous vertical order for the frame? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, §FR-025]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK025 Are the behaviours listed under *Edge Cases* traceable to functional requirements, or do several — avatar absent, name truncation, context line absent, banner outside the shell — exist only as prose no test can be traced to? [Traceability, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK026 Is behaviour specified for an avatar URL that is present but fails to load, as distinct from an avatar that is not set? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK027 Is behaviour specified when a first or last name is absent, empty or whitespace-only, given FR-017 joins exactly two parts with one space? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-017]
- [x] CHK028 Is the header context line's overflow behaviour specified, given the display name's is? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK029 Are motion and reduced-motion requirements stated, or explicitly excluded from this feature? [Coverage, Gap]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK030 Can SC-001's "changes nothing in the frame" be objectively verified, and is the set of properties it covers enumerated? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK031 Is SC-011 verifiable against a stated set of widths, including at and below the 1280px minimum? [Measurability, Spec §SC-011, §FR-010]
- [x] CHK032 Does SC-012's "every authenticated surface" scope to the surfaces this feature actually renders, or does it claim screens later entries deliver? [Clarity, Spec §SC-012]
- [x] CHK033 Is SC-010's "identically ... everywhere this feature renders it" bounded to an enumerable list of render sites? [Measurability, Spec §SC-010, §FR-017]

## Notes

- **Assisted evaluation pass, 2026-08-30.** At the reviewer's request, every item was scanned against `spec.md` and marked `[x]` only where a specific sentence in that document answered it. 32 of the 91 items across the three checklists were already satisfied; the remaining 59 were then resolved by amending `spec.md` — no requirement was added or removed, every amendment landed inside an existing FR, and the resolutions narrow `docs/product/specifications.md` rather than inventing product decisions. Where the source is silent the resolution is recorded under *Assumptions* as a default. Marks are the agent's reading and remain the reviewer's to overturn.
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Several items above ask whether a decision recorded in `plan.md` or `research.md` is also binding in `spec.md`. A decision that lives only in a design artifact is not a requirement, and a later entry reading the spec alone will not find it.
